subject: Economics
description: World Bank, IMF, ADB, WTO, NDB — roles and structure

questions.stem: The World Bank's lending arm for middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries is the:

options.option_text: IDA (International Development Association)
IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
IFC (International Finance Corporation)
MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency)

questions.explanation: World Bank Group has 5 institutions: IBRD (middle-income / creditworthy low-income country lending, the largest arm), IDA (concessional loans / grants to the poorest countries), IFC (private-sector lending), MIGA (political-risk insurance), ICSID (investment dispute settlement). 'World Bank' narrowly = IBRD + IDA. HQ — Washington DC. President is traditionally an American nominee.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: India's largest shareholder position — after the 2023 quota reforms — in the IMF is approximately:

options.option_text: 1st place
8th place
3rd place
15th place

questions.explanation: India's IMF quota share is ~2.75 % (8th among member countries, after the US, Japan, China, Germany, UK, France, Italy). A country's quota determines its voting share, borrowing access, and SDR allocation. The IMF is headquartered in Washington DC; the MD is traditionally European. Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria) is the current MD. Gita Gopinath (Indian-American) served as Chief Economist 2019-22, now Deputy MD.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The 'New Development Bank' (NDB) is a multilateral development bank set up by:

options.option_text: The G7
BRICS countries
OECD
ASEAN

questions.explanation: NDB (originally the BRICS Development Bank) — established 2015 by Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa. HQ in Shanghai; first President was K.V. Kamath of India (2015-20). Founding authorised capital of US$ 100 billion, equal shareholding. Funds infrastructure and sustainable-development projects in member and other emerging / developing countries. Intended as a complement / alternative to the Western-dominated IMF and World Bank.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has its headquarters in:

options.option_text: Tokyo
Manila
Beijing
Singapore

questions.explanation: ADB — founded 1966 — HQ in Manila, Philippines. Largest shareholders are Japan and the US (each ~15.6 %); India is a founding member. By convention, the ADB President has always been Japanese. A rival China-led institution is the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB, 2016) — HQ in Beijing, India is among its largest borrowers.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The WTO replaced which pre-existing trade body in 1995?

options.option_text: IMF
GATT
UNCTAD
OECD

questions.explanation: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1947) ran eight negotiation rounds. The Uruguay Round (1986-94) produced the Marrakesh Agreement establishing the WTO from 1 January 1995. WTO covers goods (GATT legacy), services (GATS), intellectual property (TRIPS), and has a dispute-settlement mechanism. India is a founding member. Current Director-General — Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The 'Bretton Woods Conference' of 1944 led to the creation of which two international financial institutions?

options.option_text: UN and WHO
IMF and World Bank
WTO and ADB
OECD and G7

questions.explanation: Bretton Woods (July 1944) — 44 Allied nations met at the Mount Washington Hotel, New Hampshire, to plan the post-war economic order. It created the IMF (managing exchange rates, short-term payments crises) and the IBRD / World Bank (long-term development finance). Both began operations in 1945. The Bretton Woods 'fixed but adjustable' exchange-rate system (dollar pegged to gold, others pegged to dollar) broke down in 1971 when the US ended gold convertibility.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) is:

options.option_text: A global cryptocurrency
A reserve asset whose value is based on a basket of five currencies
A form of international tax
A type of bond issued by the US Treasury

questions.explanation: SDR — created by the IMF in 1969 — is an international reserve asset that members hold in their reserves alongside gold and major currencies. Its value is set from a basket of five currencies — US dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi (added 2016), Japanese Yen, British Pound. Weights are reviewed every five years. Countries can use SDRs to settle IMF payments and swap them for hard currency with other members.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) was proposed in 2013 as an initiative of which country?

options.option_text: Japan, seeking a parallel to the ADB it already heavily funds
China, as part of its broader Belt and Road financial architecture
India, under the 2014 BRICS Fortaleza Summit framework
United States, as a complement to the existing World Bank structure

questions.explanation: China's President Xi Jinping proposed the AIIB in 2013; it was operationalised in January 2016 and is closely associated with China's Belt and Road Initiative. Option A is wrong because Japan actually boycotted AIIB initially, viewing it as a rival to the ADB (where Japan co-dominates). Option C conflates NDB (the BRICS bank established at Fortaleza 2014) with AIIB — two distinct institutions.

questions.stem: Which component of the World Bank Group extends financing directly to private-sector enterprises without requiring a government guarantee?

options.option_text: International Development Association (IDA), the soft-loan window
International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private-sector arm
Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), for political risk
International Centre for Settlement of Disputes (ICSID), arbitration

questions.explanation: The IFC is the World Bank Group's private-sector window; it provides loans, equity, and advisory services directly to companies in developing countries without a sovereign guarantee. IDA (Option A) lends to the poorest governments, not private firms. MIGA (Option C) provides guarantees against political risk but does not lend. ICSID (Option D) is an arbitration forum, not a lending body.

questions.stem: India currently holds 'Key Partner' engagement status but is NOT a full member of which major international economic organisation?

options.option_text: Asian Development Bank (ADB), based in Manila, Philippines
Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), led by China
Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
New Development Bank (NDB), the BRICS-founded institution

questions.explanation: India is not an OECD member; it has 'Key Partner' status and accession talks were formally launched in 2023. India is a founding member of ADB, AIIB, and NDB, making those distractors wrong. Candidates often confuse OECD membership because India regularly participates in OECD forums and adheres to many OECD guidelines.

questions.stem: Under the WTO's Most Favoured Nation (MFN) obligation, if a member state grants a tariff concession to any one trading partner, it must:

options.option_text: Apply the same concession immediately to all other WTO members equally
Notify the Dispute Settlement Body before extending the benefit further
Offer an equivalent concession only to least-developed country members
Publish the concession in the WTO Trade Policy Review within 30 days

questions.explanation: MFN (Article I of GATT 1994) requires non-discriminatory treatment: any advantage granted to one member must be extended unconditionally to all WTO members. Option C is the opposite — it is the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) that specifically targets developing/LDC nations, not MFN. Option B conflates MFN with DSB notification procedures, which are unrelated.

questions.stem: The Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralisation (CMIM), a regional foreign-exchange liquidity support arrangement, covers the member states of:

options.option_text: SAARC nations including India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka
ASEAN+3 grouping — ASEAN nations, China, Japan, South Korea
SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation) full-member states
BIMSTEC nations — Bay of Bengal multi-sectoral cooperation

questions.explanation: CMIM evolved from the bilateral Chiang Mai Initiative (2000) among ASEAN+3 — ten ASEAN states plus China, Japan, and South Korea — into a multilateral US$240 billion pool in 2010. It is managed by AMRO (ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office). SAARC, SCO, and BIMSTEC are separate groupings without a comparable currency-swap pool under this name.

questions.stem: In WTO terminology, domestic agricultural support classified under the 'Amber Box' is distinct because it:

options.option_text: Decoupled from production levels, hence non-trade-distorting and uncapped
Restricted to environmental schemes and rural structural programmes
Trade-distorting support subject to binding reduction commitments
Production-limiting Blue Box payments exempt from reduction schedules

questions.explanation: Amber Box support (measured by the Aggregate Measurement of Support — AMS) directly distorts production and trade, so WTO members must reduce it below bound levels. Option A describes Green Box support (decoupled, uncapped). Option D describes the Blue Box (production-limiting payments, conditionally exempt). India's food-security MSP procurement controversy at WTO revolves around whether it crosses Amber Box de minimis thresholds.

questions.stem: The Financial Stability Board (FSB), which coordinates global financial regulation across G20 jurisdictions, was created in 2009 as a successor to:

options.option_text: Bank for International Settlements (BIS) headquartered in Basel
Financial Stability Forum (FSF) founded after the 1997 Asian crisis
International Organisation of Securities Commissions (IOSCO)
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), the bank regulator

questions.explanation: The FSF was established in 1999 by G7 finance ministers after the Asian financial crisis to promote international financial stability; the G20 London Summit (2009) reformed and expanded it into the FSB with a wider membership including emerging economies like India. Option A (BIS) continues to exist and actually hosts the FSB Secretariat — it was not replaced. Option D (BCBS) remains a separate technical standard-setter under the BIS.
